title: Bioelectric patterns act as hidden layers that split the genotype–anatomy inverse problem

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Bioelectric patterns act as hidden layers that split the genotype–anatomy inverse problem

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Bioelectric networks mitigate the inverse problem of morphogenesis by acting as 'hidden layers' between genetics and anatomy: the mapping from ion channel genes to bioelectric pattern, and from bioelectric pattern to anatomy, are each easier to invert than the direct genotype–anatomy map, decomposing the control problem into two easier ones for evolution and for engineers.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2023, Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology › Bioelectric networks as reprogrammable interface to morphogenetic capabilities

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: The relationships of ion channel genes to the bioelectric pattern, and bioelectric pattern to its resulting anatomy, are each easier to invert than the direct genotype–anatomy link, so they help to decompose the control problem into two easier problems.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology”, Cellular and molecular life sciences : CMLS (2023), doi:10.1007/s00018-023-04790-z; section “Bioelectric networks as reprogrammable interface to morphogenetic capabilities”. Scope: Bioelectric control of morphogenesis in animals

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2023-agential-10: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.53

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The decomposition can be operationalized quantitatively and tested on selected systems. Existing repositories contain fragments of the required mapping, not broad matched datasets, so the general mechanism is only partially resolvable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Fit predictive and inverse models to matched ion-channel genotype, voltage-map, and anatomy data, then compare direct genotype-to-anatomy inverse error and sample complexity with a two-stage genotype-to-voltage-to-anatomy model on held-out perturbations.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Model complexity and representation can predetermine apparent invertibility.

Matched genotype, voltage, and anatomy observations are rare.

Evolutionary and engineering ease are different outcomes.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.62
analysis feasibility: 0.52
data adequacy: 0.32
data existence: 0.5
discriminating power: 0.68

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The two-step inversion comparison is a definite numerical test on a model that has both layers. Public model repositories rarely encode genotype, voltage, and anatomy together, so only a proxy analysis is available. The claim about real bioelectric control and about engineers is not settled by that proxy.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: On any public model that contains ion-channel genotype, a bioelectric pattern, and an anatomical output, compare inversion error for the direct genotype-to-anatomy map with the two-step path through the bioelectric pattern. Lower error on both steps than on the direct map would support the decomposition; equal or worse error would refute it for that model.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Easier inversion in a model is not evidence about the historical control problem faced by evolution.

Almost no deposited model contains all three layers with an invertible map.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

operationalizability: 0.55
data adequacy: 0.25
discriminating power: 0.4
data existence: 0.35
